note: Practice pack: 11+ vocabulary tasks with fixed answers. Generic content - contains no personal information.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to waste money or time when you really shouldn't'?
tasks.teach: To squander pocket money is to blow it all in one go — the show-off opposite of saving.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to tempt someone with something lovely'?
tasks.teach: The smell of warm cookies can entice anyone into the kitchen. Tempt, attract, entice — all magnets!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to officially say NO to a plan'?
tasks.teach: 'Permit' means allow — veto is its bossy opposite: one powerful NO that blocks the plan.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to stop completely'?
tasks.teach: When rain ceases, it stops. 'Cease' is a posh full stop — and 'commence' kicks things off.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a huge, noisy crowd'?
tasks.teach: A horde of fans mobbed the stage! (Sneaky cousin: 'hoard' with an A is treasure you keep.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to keep going through something hard without giving up'?
tasks.teach: Explorers endure freezing nights — they grit their teeth and carry on. You endure a very long queue!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'looking down and feeling gloomy'?
tasks.teach: Downcast eyes stare at shoes. 'Jaunty' is the happy opposite — chin up, cap at an angle!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to get in the way and slow someone down'?
tasks.teach: A pebble in your shoe hinders a runner. Its rhyme-twin 'hamper' means exactly the same!

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to run with quick little steps, like a squirrel'?
tasks.teach: Squirrels scamper, tired hikers trudge. The word sounds as quick as the feet!

tasks.prompt: A 'cryptic' message is...
tasks.teach: Cryptic = puzzling, hidden. To decipher a cryptic note is to crack its code — detective work!

tasks.prompt: Your 'visage' is your...
tasks.teach: A knight's grim visage = his stern face. Fancy word, simple meaning — examiners love it.

tasks.prompt: The sky turned a brilliant ___ over the summer sea.
tasks.teach: Azure = bright sky-blue. A painter's word — it makes a sentence glow.

tasks.prompt: The old oak's ___ branches twisted like a witch's fingers.
tasks.teach: Gnarled = twisted and knobbly. Perfect for old trees, old roots, and wizard's hands.

tasks.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?
tasks.teach: Cease, halt and stop all slam the brakes — commence starts the engine!

tasks.prompt: If you 'smell a rat', you...
tasks.teach: No actual rats involved! This idiom means 'something fishy is going on'. (Also fishy — English, honestly!)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to give way or give in'?
tasks.teach: To yield is to give way — a car yields at a junction. (It also means to produce: a field yields crops.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'one level of several stacked up'?
tasks.teach: A tier is one layer in a stack — a three-tier cake, or the tiers of seats in a stadium.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'gentle — not strong or harsh'?
tasks.teach: Mild weather is soft and gentle; a mild curry won't burn your tongue.

tasks.prompt: A large group of fish moving together is a ___.
tasks.teach: Fish swim in a shoal, birds fly in a flock, bees buzz in a swarm — collect the group words!

tasks.prompt: After the storm, the sea began to ___ into huge waves.
tasks.teach: To swell is to grow bigger — a river swells after rain, and the sea swells into waves.

tasks.prompt: She is taller ___ her brother. (comparing two things)
tasks.teach: 'Than' compares two things (bigger than). 'Then' is about time — first this, then that.

tasks.prompt: Take a deep ___ and relax. (the air you take in)
tasks.teach: 'Breath' (rhymes with death) is the air — a naming word. 'Breathe' (rhymes with seethe) is the action.

tasks.prompt: Don't ___ off the path — you'll get lost! (to roam)
tasks.teach: 'Wander' (rhymes with ponder) means to roam about. 'Wonder' means to think or to be amazed.

tasks.prompt: She had ___ amazing idea!
tasks.teach: Use 'an' before a vowel sound: an apple, an amazing idea. Use 'a' before a consonant: a book.

tasks.prompt: Which one shows the wings belonging to ONE dragon?
tasks.teach: One dragon owning something takes 's — the dragon's wings. (No apostrophe just means MORE than one dragon.)

tasks.prompt: Which sentence is joined correctly?
options: It was raining. so we stayed inside.
It was raining, we stayed inside.
It was raining we stayed inside.
It was raining, so we stayed inside.
tasks.answer: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
tasks.teach: Two whole sentences can't be glued with just a comma — pop a joining word (so, and, but) after it.

tasks.prompt: When 'she said' splits the speech, which is correct?
tasks.teach: Comma inside the first speech marks, another after 'said', then reopen the speech marks for the rest.

tasks.prompt: ___ did you put my shoes? (asking about a place)
tasks.teach: 'Where' asks about a place — it has 'here' hiding inside it. 'Were' is a doing word: they were happy.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'enormous - absolutely huge'?
tasks.teach: Immense means vast and enormous - an immense mountain seems to fill the whole sky.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'plain, strict and without comfort'?
tasks.teach: An austere room is bare and simple: one bed, one candle, no frills.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'kind and generous'?
tasks.teach: A benevolent person wishes you well and gives freely (bene = good).

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'wishing to do evil or harm'?
tasks.teach: Malevolent means wanting to cause harm - the exact opposite of benevolent (mal = bad).

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'spiteful and wanting revenge'?
tasks.teach: A vindictive person nurses a grudge and plots to get their own back.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'passionate and enthusiastic'?
tasks.teach: An ardent fan cheers with their whole heart - ardent means burning with keenness.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'silly and not serious'?
tasks.teach: Frivolous means light and silly - a frivolous idea is fun rather than important.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'completely fascinated and spellbound'?
tasks.teach: Enthralled means gripped and spellbound - so fascinated you forget everything else.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'badly built and falling apart'?
tasks.teach: A ramshackle hut leans, creaks and looks ready to collapse at any moment.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'abandoned and left to fall apart'?
tasks.teach: A derelict building has been left empty and neglected for years.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'hidden or secret'?
tasks.teach: A covert plan is secret and hidden - the opposite of 'overt', which is out in the open.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'made very poor'?
tasks.teach: Impoverished means made very poor - the long drought left the farmers impoverished.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'later than it should be'?
tasks.teach: Tardy means late - a tardy reply turns up long after you hoped for it. Its opposite is prompt, which means bang on time.

tasks.prompt: The crowd came ___ forward the moment the band walked on stage.
tasks.teach: Surging means rising and rushing forward in one powerful wave - like the sea, or a whole crowd moving at once.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'being far too pleased with yourself'?
tasks.teach: Vanity is being too proud of yourself, especially of how you look. Modesty is its quiet opposite.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a false reason given to hide the real one'?
tasks.teach: A pretext is a cover story: he called round on the pretext of returning a book, when really he wanted to see the puppy.

tasks.prompt: Three of these point outwards, towards other people. Which one points back at yourself?
tasks.teach: Egotism means thinking and talking about yourself far too much. The other three are all about noticing everybody else.

tasks.prompt: 'I have told you a million times!' Which writing technique is that?
tasks.teach: Hyperbole is enormous exaggeration for effect. (Irony says the opposite of what it means; personification treats a thing like a person; onomatopoeia sounds like its own noise, such as buzz.)

tasks.prompt: After the long walk we were ___ and ate every last sandwich.
tasks.teach: Ravenous means extremely hungry - far hungrier than merely peckish, and much too hungry to share.

tasks.prompt: Which word describes someone who is showily self-important?
tasks.teach: A pompous person puts on grand airs and rather loves the sound of their own voice. Humble is the opposite.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'perfectly peaceful and lovely'?
tasks.teach: An idyllic scene is picture-perfect and calm: a meadow, a stream and not a single worry in sight.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'completely harmless'?
tasks.teach: Innocuous means harmless - an innocuous little spider that would not hurt a fly (well, perhaps one fly).

tasks.prompt: The garden was full of ___ touches: a blue door in a tree trunk and a teapot for a birdhouse.
tasks.teach: Whimsical means playfully odd and full of imagination - charmingly not what you expected.

tasks.prompt: She took one ___ step onto the frozen pond, listening hard for a creak.
tasks.teach: Tentative means hesitant and careful, as though checking whether something is safe.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a showy display of boldness'?
tasks.teach: Bravado is swaggering and putting on a brave face, often when you feel far less brave inside.

tasks.prompt: Which word describes someone extremely mean with money?
tasks.teach: Parsimonious means unwilling to part with even a penny. A generous person is the exact opposite.

tasks.prompt: Three of these mean serious trouble. Which one means playful mischief?
tasks.teach: Shenanigans are silly goings-on and playful mischief - the sort that end in giggles rather than trouble.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a charge or tax added to goods'?
tasks.teach: A tariff is a charge or tax, and it can also mean a printed list of prices - the tariff by the ferry door tells you what a ticket costs.

tasks.prompt: The robin had only a ___ scattering of crumbs to see it through the frost.
tasks.teach: Meagre means far too small in amount - a meagre helping leaves you quietly hoping for seconds.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to explain something so that someone finally understands'?
tasks.teach: To enlighten someone is to switch a light on inside their head, so a puzzle suddenly makes sense.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to explain something in careful detail'?
tasks.teach: To expound is to set something out fully, point by point. Grandpa can expound on the proper way to brew tea for a good half hour.

tasks.prompt: Fallen leaves ___ over the winter and quietly feed the soil beneath them.
tasks.teach: To decompose is to rot and break down naturally into simpler parts, which is how a forest feeds itself.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'extra information at the back of a book'?
tasks.teach: An appendix sits at the back with the extra details. (Confusingly, you also have one inside you, and nobody is quite sure what it is for.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to light a fire, or to stir up a feeling'?
tasks.teach: You kindle a fire with small dry twigs, and a wonderful book can kindle a love of reading in just the same way.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'sensible and careful about what might happen'?
tasks.teach: A prudent person thinks ahead - packing a waterproof even when the sky looks perfectly innocent.

tasks.prompt: In old poems, 'the ether' means...
tasks.teach: Ether is an old, poetic word for the clear air high above the clouds. (It was also the name of an early anaesthetic.)

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to run away secretly, usually in order to marry'?
tasks.teach: To elope is to slip away quietly and marry without the big planned wedding - a great favourite in old novels.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'terrible destruction'?
tasks.teach: Carnage means dreadful destruction. People use it lightly too: after the storm the beach was carnage, all snapped umbrellas and cross seagulls.

tasks.prompt: The twins ___ their uncle completely, and he never realised they had swapped places.
tasks.teach: To be hoodwinked is to be tricked or fooled. It comes from the old trick of pulling a hood over somebody's eyes.

tasks.prompt: 'The drought took a heavy toll on the crops.' Here, toll means...
options: the cost in damage or suffering
tasks.answer: the cost in damage or suffering
tasks.teach: A toll is what something costs you, often in harm. (A toll is also a charge to cross a bridge, and the slow ringing of a bell.)

tasks.prompt: Calling the largest dog in the park 'Tiny' is an example of...
tasks.teach: Irony is saying the opposite of what you mean, so the listener hears both at once - and usually smiles.

tasks.prompt: 'The wind whispered secrets to the trees.' Which technique is that?
tasks.teach: Personification treats a thing as though it were a person. Wind cannot really whisper, which is exactly what makes the line lovely.

tasks.prompt: Buzz, splash and crunch are all examples of...
tasks.teach: Onomatopoeia is a word that sounds like the noise it names. You can hear the meaning as you say it.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'not caring at all'?
tasks.teach: Apathy is a complete shrug: no interest, no energy, no caring either way.

tasks.prompt: The ___ of the lake at dawn was broken only by two geese landing on it.
tasks.teach: Tranquillity is deep calm and peacefulness. Watch the double l in the middle: tranquillity.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'celebration and merrymaking'?
tasks.teach: Festivity is the happy noise of a celebration: lanterns, fiddles and far too many cakes.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'being unknown, or hard to make out'?
tasks.teach: Obscurity means being unnoticed or unclear. A painter can live in obscurity for years before the galleries finally queue up.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'only on the surface'?
tasks.teach: Superficial means surface-level only. A superficial scratch needs a plaster and a biscuit, and nothing more.

tasks.prompt: Three of these mean taking sides. Which one means being fair to everybody?
tasks.teach: Objective means judging fairly, without favouring anyone. A good referee stays objective however loudly the crowd shouts.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'strongly unfriendly'?
tasks.teach: Hostile means unfriendly and opposed. A hostile stare says 'you are not welcome here' without a single word.

tasks.prompt: The rain was ___ all weekend, so we built a den indoors instead.
tasks.teach: Relentless means never stopping or easing off - it simply keeps coming, hour after hour.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'an award or high praise'?
tasks.teach: An accolade is public praise or an award - the highest accolade in her whole sport.

tasks.prompt: Which word describes a face showing no emotion at all?
tasks.teach: An impassive face gives nothing away, however much is going on behind it.

tasks.prompt: Thick mud began to ___ their progress up the hill.
tasks.teach: To impede is to get in the way and slow something down.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'to complain about something'?
tasks.teach: To bemoan is to grumble aloud about something. Gardeners bemoan the weather in every season going.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'very high, or grand and superior'?
tasks.teach: Lofty means towering high. It also describes grand ideas, or somebody with a rather superior manner.

tasks.prompt: She felt her heart ___ as the first firework whistled upwards.
tasks.teach: To palpitate is to beat fast and flutter - the word your heart deserves at a thrilling moment.

tasks.prompt: Three of these describe towns and cities. Which one describes the countryside?
tasks.teach: Rural means to do with the countryside. Urban is its opposite, meaning to do with cities.

tasks.prompt: If two lists 'correspond', they...
tasks.teach: To correspond is to match up. It also means to write letters to somebody over a long stretch of time.

tasks.prompt: Which word means 'a soft whispering or rustling sound'?
tasks.teach: Susurration is the gentlest word in English for a whisper of leaves or distant voices. It even sounds like the sound it names.

tasks.prompt: If something is 'uniform', it is...
options: the same all the way through
tasks.answer: the same all the way through
tasks.teach: Uniform means unvarying, the same throughout. That is why school uniform has its name - everybody matches.
